title: Time & work
examples: If two people work together, how do I find their combined rate?
What is the difference between working together and working sequentially?
Can I use this concept for anything other than pipes?

explain.say: Today we are looking at combined work rates. This means finding how fast multiple people work together.
If person A takes four hours and person B takes six hours. Their individual rates are one divided by four and one divided by six.
To find the combined rate, we add these individual rates together. So we add one divided by four and one divided by six.
The combined rate is two divided by twelve plus one divided by twelve. This equals three divided by twelve, which simplifies to one divided by four.
If the combined rate is one divided by four, the total time taken is the reciprocal. So the time taken is four hours.
For pipes and cisterns, the concept is the same. If one pipe fills in three hours and another empties in five hours. We add the filling rate and subtract the emptying rate.

faq.q: Do I always add the rates when working together?
faq.a: Yes, when people or pipes work together, you add their individual rates to find the combined rate.
asks: Is it always addition for combined work?

faq.q: What if one pipe is emptying the cistern?
faq.a: If a pipe is emptying, you must subtract its rate from the filling rate. This gives you the net rate.
asks: How do I handle an emptying pipe?
Do I change the sign for emptying?

faq.q: Should I calculate the rates in terms of units per hour?
faq.a: Yes, keeping the units consistent, like fraction of the job per hour, is very important for accuracy.
asks: What are the units for the rate?
Can I use liters per minute instead?

faq.q: Does the total time calculation change if I use the LCM method?
faq.a: The final time calculation is always the reciprocal of the net rate, regardless of the method used to find the rate.
asks: What is the final step after finding the combined rate?

faq.q: Can I use this for more than two workers?
faq.a: Yes, you simply add the rates of all the workers or pipes involved to find the total combined rate.
asks: What if there are three people?
How do I add three rates together?

facts: Work Rate is the inverse of the time taken to complete the job.
When combining workers, rates are added together.
When one pipe empties, its rate is subtracted from the filling rate.
The final time taken is the reciprocal of the net combined rate.

quiz.say: A can paint a room in 3 hours, and B can paint it in 6 hours. How long together?
quiz.why: Combined rate is 1/3 + 1/6, which equals 3/6 or 1/2. The time taken is the reciprocal of 1/2, which is 2 hours.

wrong.0: This is the combined rate, not the time taken. You must take the reciprocal.
wrong.1: This is the sum of the times (3 + 6), which is incorrect for combined work.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the sum of the rates without finding the final time.

quiz.say: Pipe X fills a tank in 4 hours, and Pipe Y empties it in 6 hours. Time together?
quiz.why: The net rate is 1/4 minus 1/6, which equals 1/12. The time taken is the reciprocal of 1/12, which is 12 hours.

wrong.0: This is the net rate, but the question asks for the total time, which requires taking the reciprocal.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the rates together instead of subtracting the emptying rate.
wrong.3: This is the sum of the times (4 + 6), ignoring the emptying action.

quiz.say: If A takes 2 hours and B takes 3 hours, what is the combined rate?
quiz.why: You must add the rates: 1/2 plus 1/3 equals 3/6 plus 2/6, which is 5/6. This is the rate, not the time.

wrong.0: This incorrectly subtracts the rates instead of adding them together.
wrong.1: This incorrectly adds the times together, which does not represent the rate.
wrong.2: This uses an incorrect common denominator for the addition of the two rates.
